newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Strong Israel will always protect Jews - Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Strong Israel will always protect Jews - Netanyahu.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu promised on Sunday that a strong Israel would always ensure the atrocities of World War II, when Nazis exterminated six million Jews, never recur.
"Never again will Jewish children be helpless," said Netanyahu, speaking at an annual ceremony in Jerusalem to mark the Holocaust.

"Today we promise them, survivors and victims alike, that we shall dedicate our lives to ensure that the danger of annihilation never hovers over our children's head, that they shall never know terror or fear, nor die an untimely death.
"Today we vow that we will maintain a strong Israel, that we shall achieve peace for our people and that we shall give our children and grandchildren security and hope," Netanyahu said.
Flags throughout Israel were at half-mast at the start of the 24-hour memorial and Israeli television showed footage from Nazi death camps where Jews were systematically exterminated.
Adolf Hitler began persecuting Jews after seizing power in Germany in 1933 but the slaughter of Jews known as the Nazis' "Final Solution" began in the early years of World War II.
Israel, established three years after that conflict, has an armed force thought to be equipped with nuclear weapons, and has fought several wars with Arab neighbours.
Some 2,500 young Jews from around the world on Sunday marked the Holocaust by staging a March of the Living at the site of Nazi Germany's biggest death camp in southern Poland.

The youths, mainly from Israel, Canada and the United States, marched from the site of the former Auschwitz concentration camp in the town of Oswiecim to nearby Birkenau, where most of the complex's 1.5 million victims were killed.
About 90 percent of those put to death in the Auschwitz-Birkenau complex were Jewish, many of them brought in from all over Europe.

The War atrocities were also marked in Paris where relatives of death camp victims and members of Jewish youth groups gathered at a square dedicated to the memory of wartime concentration camp dead and read aloud the names of 76,000 Jews deported from France. A similar ceremony was held in Berlin.
Earlier, Jewish groups said violence against Jews had waned worldwide in the last year but hate groups were increasingly turning to the Internet to spread anti-Semitism.

"Hate groups which are quite marginalised in society and found it difficult to disseminate anti-Semitism now have the potential to reach hundreds of thousands, if not millions, on their websites," said Harry Wall of the U.S.-based Anti-Defamation League, which helped produce the report.
It found that major attacks -- defined as shootings, firebombs and arson -- against Jews declined worldwide from 41 in 1995 to 32 last year.

"Not all the reasons for this decline are discernible...yet one might assume that in part it is the result of more stringent enforcement of existing and new anti-racist and anti-terrorist laws," the report said.
It listed 39 World Wide Web sites it considered anti-Semitic and said many were placed on free or individual homepages provided by companies that link computer users to the Internet.
